messages:
alex: Quick sync — BetaCare asked to bump their p99 SLO from 350ms -> 200ms for their pilot. They want this by end of next sprint. Can we scope?

maria: 200ms p99 is tight on our current hosted config for gen-heavy traffic. Options: 1) route BetaCare to a dedicated small pool (fast, higher $), 2) soft-batching limits + KV prefix cache tuning (low effort, medium win), 3) model quantization & kernel tuning (high effort, long lead).

taylor: CS input: BetaCare said they'd sign a paid SLA for 250ms. 200ms is their ideal, but they can be flexible if we ship concrete improvements quickly.

alex: Thinking we should run a quick prioritization (RICE-ish) and propose sequencing. @maria can you give rough effort and confidence numbers?

maria: Effort estimates (rough): batching/cache changes ~ 3 dev-days + 1 day QA, confidence 0.7. Dedicated routing (customer-specific) ~ 2 dev-days infra + config + cost modeling, confidence 0.9. Quant/compilation work ~ 6-8 sprints across teams (runtime + eval), confidence 0.3.

alex: Rough RICE mental model: impact weighted by pilot importance but also by cross-customer reach. For BetaCare only, reach is small; batching/cache has broader reach. So prioritization likely: 1) batching/cache (fast, broad), 2) dedicated-paid pool for BetaCare (fast, targeted), 3) quantization (big impact but long).

sam: From an ops perspective: dedicated pool will give predictable latency but raises unit costs and capacity planning. Batching + KV cache reduces per-token compute and helps cost for everyone — good long-term ROI. Also watch throughput: aggressive batching can hurt tail latency if not traffic-aware.

taylor: Sales ask: can we commit to launch criteria for the pilot? They want p99 <=250ms as a measurable goal and a rollback policy if regressions show up. Also want a simple canary test for BetaCare traffic.

maria: I can get batching + cache config live in ~10 working days if we prioritize it in the sprint. With temporary traffic shaping + routing, 250ms p99 looks achievable. 200ms may require the paid dedicated option or deeper model work.

alex: Proposed decision: 1) Prioritize batching/cache changes in next sprint (ticket in product board). 2) Offer BetaCare a paid dedicated pool as an interim SLA to hit 200ms if they require it immediately. 3) Put quant/compilation on Q2 roadmap as a strategic investment. 4) Define launch criteria for pilot: p99 <=250ms, no quality regression on eval set, canary traffic for 48h. Thoughts?

taylor: +1 from CS, I'll draft the concession and SLA language and loop legal. Will flag if they push hard for 200ms guaranteed.

maria: +1. Ping me when the ticket is created and before we flip routing so we can validate cache hit rates + metrics.

alex: Thanks — I'll create the sprint ticket and add the RICE notes + estimates. We'll update BetaCare by EOD with the plan and a clear set of launch criteria. :thumbsup:
